# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The company has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage.

The Client has three AI use cases at different stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Client targets ISO/IEC 42001, with work expected to start next year and no fixed start date. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function.

The stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." Three constraints apply:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A conventional consulting engagement would produce a governance system on the Client's behalf and leave it with the Client at the end. The Guided AI GRC Build works the other way. The Client's own build team drafts, adopts and runs each artifact during the program, supported by weekly workshops and coaching. At Week 12 the people who will operate the AI Management System (AIMS) are the people who built it. They understand why each control exists and can maintain the system without depending on outside authors.

This matters for Tamarack Instruments for three reasons:

1. **Existing management systems.** The Client already runs an ISMS, a quality management system and an internal audit function. An AIMS built inside the organization can be designed to sit alongside those systems rather than beside them as a separate structure.
2. **Evidence in the Client's own records.** Any future ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work will rely on evidence that the system operates in practice. A guided build starts that evidence in the Client's own records from Week 8.
3. **Human accountability.** The program is grounded in three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. A team that builds its own governance holds the accountability that the third principle requires.

The program uses two open frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)

Steering outputs can draw on AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) where board-level reporting is needed.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory sequencing for Weeks 2 to 5:**

1. **Customer service chatbot first.** It is the only deployed system and it sits on a customer-facing portal.
2. **AI visual inspection second.** It is the system named in the stated objective, and governance needs to be in place before it moves toward production.
3. **AI sales forecasting third.** It is entered as a planned system so that it passes through intake governance before deployment rather than after.

Any further AI systems in use across the business are `Unknown`. Week 2 includes a discovery sweep to surface them.

**Integration points.** Integration with the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 quality management system is `Unknown` for each week, because the specific artifacts these systems would attach to are not yet identified. Identifying those artifacts is a Week 1 intake question. The one stated artifact is the June 2026 internal audit finding, which the Week 2 inventory addresses directly.

**ISO/IEC 42001 mapping.** The readiness themes below show how each week's artifacts relate to ISO/IEC 42001 clause themes. They describe readiness only. The program does not promise certification or any audit outcome.

| Week | Focus | Tailoring for Tamarack Instruments | ISO/IEC 42001 readiness theme | Integration point |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles | AIMS charter and scope across the Netherlands, Germany and the United States; works council consultation planning | Context; Leadership | Unknown |
| 2 | AI system inventory | Chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting entered first; discovery sweep for others | Context; Operation | June 2026 internal audit finding |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology | Each system assessed against EU AI Act categories | Planning | Unknown |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments | Chatbot and visual inspection assessed first; GDPR impact assessment need reviewed | Planning; Operation | Unknown |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Treatment plans for the first assessed systems | Planning | Unknown |
| 6 | Policy set and mid-point steering | Core AI policy set drafted for adoption | Leadership; Support | Unknown |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle gates covering pilot to production for visual inspection | Operation | Unknown |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection begins | Supplier review against the EU customer data residency constraint | Operation; Support | Unknown |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight (Slow AI Kitchen) | At least two workflows designed for production use | Operation | Unknown |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring | Monitoring criteria for systems in production use | Performance evaluation | Unknown |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Incident and change procedures; first evidence review | Operation; Improvement | Unknown |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Readiness review with the internal auditors on the build team | Performance evaluation; Improvement | Unknown |

**Items with legal effect.** The following items have legal effect: confirm with external counsel.

- EU AI Act classification outcomes in Week 3.
- GDPR impact assessment determinations in Week 4.
- Data residency findings in Week 8.
- Works council consultation obligations throughout the program.

**Questions to confirm at intake:**

- Does the customer service chatbot process customer personal data?
- Where is that data stored?
- Does the visual inspection pilot touch production staff, which would bring in works council consultation?

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a functioning minimum viable AIMS, defined as:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

The customer service chatbot is the deployed candidate for the governed workflow requirement. The second workflow is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake. Whether visual inspection reaches production use within the program period is `Unknown`. The program will govern its path to production either way.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

All figures below are **estimates**, not commitments or actuals. Each role attends the weekly workshop (estimate: 2 hours) and the weekly coaching session (estimate: 1 hour). The remaining time is asynchronous implementation.

| Role | Estimated hours per week | Estimated peak weeks |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 4 to 6 | 1, 3, 6, 12 |
| CISO | 4 to 6 | 4, 8, 11 |
| Head of Quality | 5 to 7 | 7, 10, 11 |
| Head of Data | 5 to 7 | 2, 4, 10 |
| German plant manager | 3 to 5 | Unknown; to confirm at intake |
| Internal auditors (two), each | 4 to 6 | 8, 11, 12 |

Estimated peak weeks may rise by 2 to 3 hours per role. Confirmed allocations will be agreed in Week 1.

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at three points:

- **Week 1:** mobilization, scope and decisions needed.
- **Week 6:** mid-point status, blockers and scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** minimum viable AIMS attestation against the six-element definition and a 12-month operating plan.

Steering attendance is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

## 7. Logistics and Price

**Format.** Each week includes one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation between sessions. Session times will be set at intake once participant locations are confirmed.

**Price.** US$60,000 for the full twelve-week program. This sits within the stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. Whether the fiscal year boundary falls within the program period is a question to confirm at intake.

**Start date.** The start date is not yet set. As an illustration, a program beginning in the first full week of January 2027 would reach Week 12 in late March 2027, before Q2 2027. A start date and schedule will be confirmed at intake.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The proposed next step is a 60-minute intake session to:

- confirm the open questions in this proposal
- identify the ISMS and quality management system artifacts that serve as integration points
- agree the second governed workflow candidate
- set the Week 1 date

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
